root_dir <- here::here()

# load required packages (adapt to your environment)
library(Seurat)

1. Introduction

This report summarizes an end-to-end, fully reproducible single-cell RNA-seq workflow for the Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) dataset GSE161529, comparing TNBC tumor cells with normal epithelial cells.

The pipeline follows these main stages:

Quality control and filtering of raw 10X data

Data integration of TNBC and normal epithelial samples

Cell type annotation using SingleR and breast-epithelial reference data

Cluster marker identification

Pseudobulk differential expression (DE) with edgeR

Functional enrichment analysis of DE genes

Copy number variation (CNV) analysis using CopyKAT (optional)

All heavy lifting is implemented in modular R scripts under the R/ folder.
This R Markdown file simply sources those scripts and organizes the results into a single, human-readable report.

2. Data loading and quality control
Writing
This script should:
- read raw 10X data
- create a Seurat object (e.g., seurat_obj)
- perform QC and filtering

source(file.path(r_dir, "01_load_qc.R"))

If your script saves the object instead, e.g. to results/seurat_qc.rds, load it here:
seurat_obj <- readRDS(file.path(res_dir, "seurat_qc.rds"))
Basic QC summary (adapt to your actual object name)

seurat_obj

Writing
Example QC plots (modify according to your object names / metadata)

VlnPlot(seurat_obj, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)

3. Integration of TNBC and normal epithelial datasets
Writing
This script should:
- perform normalization and feature selection
- integrate TNBC + normal epithelium using Seurat RPCA (or similar)
- run PCA, UMAP, clustering

source(file.path(r_dir, "02_integration.R"))

If integration results are saved as RDS:
seurat_integrated <- readRDS(file.path(res_dir, "seurat_integrated.rds"))

seurat_integrated

Writing

DimPlot(seurat_integrated, reduction = "umap", group.by = "sample_type", pt.size = 0.3) +
ggtitle("UMAP: TNBC vs Normal epithelial cells")

4. Cell type annotation (SingleR)
Writing
This script should:
- run SingleR using a breast-epithelial reference (e.g., celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData)
- add cell type labels to metadata (e.g., seurat_integrated$celltype)

source(file.path(r_dir, "03_annotation_SingleR.R"))

Example cell-type UMAP

DimPlot(seurat_integrated, group.by = "celltype", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, pt.size = 0.3) +
ggtitle("UMAP colored by SingleR-derived cell types")

5. Cluster markers
Writing
This script should:
- identify cluster-specific markers (e.g., FindAllMarkers)
- save results as a table in results/markers_TNBC_vs_normal.csv

source(file.path(r_dir, "04_markers.R"))

markers_path <- file.path(res_dir, "markers_TNBC_vs_normal.csv")
if (file.exists(markers_path)) {
markers_tbl <- data.table::fread(markers_path)
head(markers_tbl)
}

Writing
Example marker visualization (adapt gene names / cluster IDs)

FeaturePlot(seurat_integrated, features = c("KRT8", "KRT18"), cols = c("lightgrey", "red"), pt.size = 0.3) &
theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

6. Pseudobulk differential expression (edgeR)
Writing
This script should:
- aggregate counts by sample / condition
- run edgeR for TNBC vs Normal
- save DE results (e.g., results/edgeR_DE_TNBC_vs_Normal.csv)

source(file.path(r_dir, "05_de_pseudobulk_edgeR.R"))

de_path <- file.path(res_dir, "edgeR_DE_TNBC_vs_Normal.csv")
if (file.exists(de_path)) {
de_tbl <- data.table::fread(de_path)
head(de_tbl[order(FDR)][1:10])
}

Writing
Simple volcano plot (adapt column names if needed)

if (exists("de_tbl")) {
de_tbl$log10FDR <- -log10(de_tbl$FDR + 1e-300)
ggplot(de_tbl, aes(logFC, log10FDR)) +
geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
labs(
x = "log2 fold change (TNBC vs Normal)",
y = "-log10(FDR)",
title = "Pseudobulk DE: TNBC vs Normal epithelial cells"
) +
theme_minimal()
}

7. Functional enrichment analysis
Writing
This script should:
- perform GO / pathway enrichment on significant DE genes
- save results in results/enrichment_GO_BP_TNBC.csv (or similar)

source(file.path(r_dir, "06_enrichment_analysis.R"))

enr_path <- file.path(res_dir, "enrichment_GO_BP_TNBC.csv")
if (file.exists(enr_path)) {
enr_tbl <- data.table::fread(enr_path)
head(enr_tbl)
}

Writing

if (exists("enr_tbl")) {
top_enr <- enr_tbl[1(10, .N)]
ggplot(top_enr, aes(x = reorder(Term, Combined.Score), y = Combined.Score)) +
geom_col() +
coord_flip() +
labs(
x = "GO Biological Process",
y = "Combined score",
title = "Top enriched GO BP terms (TNBC vs Normal)"
) +
theme_minimal()
}

8. CNV analysis (CopyKAT – optional)
Writing
CopyKAT can be computationally intensive; this chunk is disabled by default.
To run CNV analysis, set eval=TRUE above and make sure CopyKAT is installed.

source(file.path(r_dir, "07_cnv_analysis.R"))

Depending on your script, you might produce:
- CNV heatmaps
- classification of cells as diploid vs aneuploid
Writing
Example placeholder for a CNV heatmap figure produced by CopyKAT
knitr::include_graphics("results/cnv_heatmap_TNBC.png")
9. Reproducibility notes

All analysis steps are:

Defined in modular R scripts under the R/ folder.

Orchestrated through this R Markdown report.

Designed so that all tables and figures can be regenerated by re-running the pipeline from the raw data.

To re-run the full workflow from the command line:

Rscript R/01_load_qc.R
Rscript R/02_integration.R
Rscript R/03_annotation_SingleR.R
Rscript R/04_markers.R
Rscript R/05_de_pseudobulk_edgeR.R
Rscript R/06_enrichment_analysis.R
Rscript R/07_cnv_analysis.R   # optional


Or simply knit this report:

rmarkdown::render("TNBC_scRNAseq_report.Rmd")


This will recreate all intermediate objects, figures, and summary tables in the results/ directory (if you choose to keep it Git-ignored) or in memory during knitting.
